name: Mac mini with M6
official_support: Apple announced M6 Mac mini on August 25, 2026. Apple says M6 has a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, 16GB unified memory standard configurable to 32GB, up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth, macOS 27, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet with a 10Gb option, Wi-Fi 7, and Bluetooth 6.
local_ai_fit: Good entry local-inference and always-on agent host when configured with 24GB or 32GB memory. Best for small-to-medium quantized models, Ollama experiments, Open WebUI, Hermes/OpenClaw with cloud providers, and lightweight local models. Do not treat the Neural Engine as automatic support for every third-party LLM runtime.
memory: 16GB standard; configure 24GB or 32GB for local models and concurrent services.
storage: Choose enough internal storage for macOS, models, logs, and containers; external Thunderbolt/USB SSD can extend capacity, but model loading and backup workflows should be tested.
os: macOS 27 announced with the product; verify runtime release support before relying on a new OS on day one.
thermal: Compact, low-noise desktop intended for continuous use; sustained model load, room temperature, and enclosure airflow still affect throttling.

service_fit.Hermes Agent: documented platform support for macOS; local terminal is feasible; model execution depends on provider/runtime
service_fit.OpenClaw: documented macOS gateway support; suitable as an always-on gateway if sleep, updates, network, and permissions are managed
service_fit.Ollama: Apple Silicon path is supported by Ollama; current MLX acceleration claims are preview/version-specific
service_fit.LM Studio: official requirements require Apple Silicon and macOS 14+; new M6 should be checked against the current release
service_fit.Open WebUI: runs as a local/containerized web UI; model workload is primarily in Ollama or another backend

unresolved: Apple's public technical-specifications page returned older M4/M4 Pro material during this check while the August 25 newsroom announcement describes M6/M5 Pro. Treat the newsroom announcement as the dated launch source and re-check the specifications page before publishing exact port, memory, storage, or configuration claims.
Third-party Ollama, LM Studio, and agent support on M6 should be confirmed against releases that explicitly support the chip and macOS 27.
Apple's performance claims are vendor test claims, not an independent benchmark for every model or runtime.
recommendation: Best compact Apple choice for a quiet always-on agent gateway plus modest local inference; choose 32GB if local models matter more than basic gateway work.

name: Mac mini with M5 Pro
official_support: Apple announced M5 Pro Mac mini on August 25, 2026. Apple says it scales up to an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU, supports up to 64GB unified memory with 307GB/s bandwidth, includes Neural Accelerators, Thunderbolt 5, macOS 27, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and 2.5Gb Ethernet with a 10Gb option.
local_ai_fit: Strong compact local-AI option for larger quantized models and concurrent agent/UI workloads, subject to the chosen memory configuration and runtime support. It is not equivalent to a discrete 24GB/32GB GPU for every CUDA workload.
memory: Up to 64GB unified memory according to Apple announcement; prefer 48GB or 64GB for larger local models and multiple services.
storage: Prefer 1TB or more if keeping several model families, containers, embeddings, and backups locally; external Thunderbolt 5 storage is a useful expansion path.
os: macOS 27 announced with the product; check current runtime compatibility before production use.
thermal: Apple positions it for demanding sustained workflows and always-on agentic computing; actual sustained inference behavior needs independent testing.

service_fit.Hermes Agent: good host for macOS agent workflows, with local, Docker, SSH, or cloud execution boundaries
service_fit.OpenClaw: good dedicated gateway candidate; pair with cloud models or a local backend depending on memory and runtime
service_fit.Ollama: strong Apple Silicon candidate; confirm current MLX/GGUF support and model-specific memory fit
service_fit.LM Studio: likely suitable once release support is confirmed; official app requirements currently cover Apple Silicon
service_fit.Open WebUI: good UI host when paired with a separately tested local model backend

unresolved: Exact base memory/storage combinations and current purchase-configurator availability need confirmation from Apple's live store/specifications page.
No independent tokens-per-second or thermals were found in the official announcement.
Unified memory is shared by CPU/GPU/system; usable model memory is lower than installed memory after macOS and other processes.
recommendation: The most compelling new Mac mini tier for local models plus always-on agent services, if the 48GB/64GB configurations fit the budget.

name: Mac Studio with M5 Max or M5 Ultra
official_support: Apple announced M5 Max and M5 Ultra Mac Studio on August 25, 2026. Apple describes up to 128GB unified memory on M5 Max and up to 512GB on M5 Ultra, with Thunderbolt 5 and high memory bandwidth for large on-device AI models.
local_ai_fit: Best Apple option in this coverage for very large local models and multi-service workloads, but software support, model format, memory bandwidth, and model license remain decisive. A large memory pool does not guarantee acceptable speed.
memory: Apple announcement: up to 128GB M5 Max and 512GB M5 Ultra. Configure for the model class and concurrency actually planned.
storage: Prefer 1TB or more plus fast external storage for model libraries and datasets; keep backups separate.
os: macOS 27 announced with the new generation; verify runtime support before production deployment.
thermal: Designed for sustained pro workloads with active cooling; power, noise, and electricity cost exceed a Mac mini.

service_fit.Hermes Agent: excellent host for agent orchestration and local/remote execution, provided permissions are isolated
service_fit.OpenClaw: excellent dedicated gateway or multi-agent host; local models require separate runtime validation
service_fit.Ollama: strong candidate for large local models; benchmark the exact model and quantization
service_fit.LM Studio: Apple Silicon support is documented; verify current release against the new chips
service_fit.Open WebUI: strong host for personal/small-team local UI, with database/storage scaling limits still relevant

unresolved: Exact M5 Max/M5 Ultra configuration and late-October 512GB availability must be checked in Apple's live store.
Apple's announcement does not establish third-party runtime performance for every model.
Large local-model support depends on quantization, context length, KV cache, and runtime memory behavior.
recommendation: Choose only when large local models or heavy concurrent workloads justify the cost; otherwise a 32GB/64GB Mac mini or discrete-GPU PC is easier to justify.

name: NVIDIA RTX 5090 desktop workstation
official_support: NVIDIA lists 32GB GDDR7, an 850W minimum power recommendation, three-slot physical clearance, and a 304mm card length for the reference design. Actual add-in-card specifications vary.
local_ai_fit: Best mainstream single-GPU option here for CUDA-first local inference, image/video generation, and applications that benefit from dedicated VRAM. The 32GB VRAM ceiling still constrains unquantized and very large models.
memory: 32GB dedicated VRAM; system RAM of 64GB is a sensible workstation target for local AI, containers, datasets, and browser/agent overhead.
storage: Use a fast NVMe SSD; 2TB is a practical starting point for multiple model families and containers.
os: Windows and Linux are common deployment targets; verify driver, CUDA, WSL2, and application support for the chosen stack.
thermal: Requires a properly ventilated case, substantial PSU, and adequate cooling. Check exact card dimensions, connector clearance, and sustained-load noise.

service_fit.Hermes Agent: good on Linux/Windows paths when terminal, Docker, or WSL boundaries are configured; GPU use depends on the model backend
service_fit.OpenClaw: gateway itself is lightweight; RTX workstation is useful when paired with a local model server
service_fit.Ollama: strong fit for NVIDIA GPU workloads when current driver/runtime support is installed
service_fit.LM Studio: official Windows guidance recommends at least 4GB dedicated VRAM; 32GB provides substantially more headroom
service_fit.Open WebUI: good UI host paired with Ollama/compatible GPU backends; Docker CUDA image is documented

unresolved: NVIDIA's official page did not expose a reliable current street price in this check.
Partner cards differ in dimensions, cooling, power connectors, and warranty.
Application-specific CUDA/driver support should be checked before purchase.
recommendation: Best choice for CUDA-heavy local AI and generation workflows when power, heat, and desktop size are acceptable.

name: Raspberry Pi 5 (8GB or 16GB) gateway
official_support: Raspberry Pi lists a 2.4GHz quad-core Cortex-A76 CPU, 1GB/2GB/4GB/8GB/16GB RAM variants, Gigabit Ethernet, PCIe 2.0 x1, USB 3, and recommends a 5V/5A USB-C supply and active cooling for Pi 5 workloads. The official page lists the 16GB model at $305 during this check.
local_ai_fit: Excellent low-power always-on gateway for OpenClaw with cloud models, lightweight webhooks, messaging, and remote orchestration. Not a sensible primary host for modern local LLM inference; use it as a control plane and point models elsewhere.
memory: 4GB is enough for a simple gateway; 8GB is a comfortable target; 16GB is unnecessary for most gateway-only deployments.
storage: Prefer USB SSD or an M.2 SSD over a heavily written microSD card for state, logs, and databases.
os: 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS is the documented path; OpenClaw documents ARM64 support and Raspberry Pi deployment.
thermal: Use active cooling and the official 27W supply for sustained operation; under-powering or passive cooling can reduce reliability.

service_fit.Hermes Agent: possible for lightweight control tasks if dependencies and platform support fit; remote terminal backends may be more practical
service_fit.OpenClaw: official documentation describes Pi 4/5 gateway deployment; ideal for cloud-model gateway use
service_fit.Ollama: not recommended as the main host for modern model families because CPU/RAM limits dominate
service_fit.LM Studio: not a target desktop platform in LM Studio's documented macOS/Windows/Linux requirements
service_fit.Open WebUI: possible as a small ARM64 service, but model inference and database/storage load should be kept modest

unresolved: Retailer stock and regional pricing change frequently.
OpenClaw's gateway requirements do not mean every optional skill binary has an ARM64 build.
Open WebUI ARM deployment and extension compatibility should be tested before team use.
recommendation: Buy for an inexpensive always-on gateway, not for serious local model inference.
